title: Augmented analytics tools that push AI insights to email and Slack (2026): 8 BI platforms compared
summary: Tableau Pulse, ThoughtSpot, Omni, Databricks Genie, and Basedash push AI-written insights; compare setup, cadence, Slack delivery, permissions, and price.
body_markdown:
Eight BI platforms push AI-generated insights to people without anyone opening a dashboard, but they work in three different ways. Tableau Pulse, ThoughtSpot, and AWS Quick Sight watch metrics you define and send statistical findings with an AI-written summary. Omni, Databricks Genie, and Power BI run a prompt or report you set up on a schedule and email the written answer. Basedash Insights is the only one in this set that needs neither metrics nor a prompt: it picks what to report from your connected data and posts it to email and Slack.


Settled KPIs suit metric digests, changing questions suit scheduled prompts, and the trend nobody thought to track needs a tool that looks on its own.


## How we evaluated augmented analytics tools


“Augmented analytics” covers any BI feature where machine learning or a language model does part of the analyst’s job. This guide narrows it to insights that are pushed: delivered to an inbox, Slack, Teams, or a phone on a schedule or trigger. On-demand features like chat and “explain this chart” are noted but not scored.


We checked each vendor’s official documentation and pricing pages on November 14, 2026, against five criteria:


1. **Setup required:** do you define metrics, write a prompt, configure an alert, or nothing?
2. **How findings are produced:** deterministic statistics, machine learning, a language model, or a mix, and whether the tool explains which drivers moved a number.
3. **Triggers and channels:** digest cadence, condition or data-change triggers, and delivery to email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, webhooks, or mobile.
4. **Permissions:** whether a pushed insight respects each recipient’s row-level security or runs as one account.
5. **Plan and price:** which edition includes the feature, extra AI charges, and the published starting price.

## Tableau Pulse: best for metric digests that every viewer can receive


**Best for:** Tableau Cloud customers who want governed metrics delivered to a large audience. **Not ideal for:** teams on Tableau Server or with no metric definitions yet.


[Tableau Pulse](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_about.htm) sends each user a digest of the metrics they follow. A creator first builds metric definitions on a single published data source. Pulse then runs[deterministic statistical models](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_insights_platform_insight_types.htm) for period-over-period change, unexpected values, trend changes, outliers, and top drivers and detractors. Tableau’s documentation states that AI “isn’t involved in the identification of data insights” and only writes the[summary at the top of each digest](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_set_up.htm) , with checks that no numbers change.


- **Pricing:** Pulse is listed on Tableau Standard, which starts at $15/user/month billed annually, and Enterprise at $35 ([pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/teams-orgs) , verified November 14, 2026). Tableau Agent in Pulse, correlated metrics, and forecasts need[Tableau+](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_capabilities.htm) . The Tableau Cloud trial includes Pulse.
- **Cadence and channels:** digests go out[daily, weekly, or monthly](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_explore_metrics.htm) by email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.[Alerts](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_alerts.htm) are checked once every 24 hours and also arrive as mobile notifications.
- **Deployment and data:** Tableau Cloud only. Metrics run on extracts or live connections, including Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and PostgreSQL.
- **Security:** metrics respect row-level security on the data source; SAML and[SCIM](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/scim_config_online.htm) are supported.
- **Embedding:** a[<tableau-pulse> web component](https://help.tableau.com/current/api/embedding_api/en-us/docs/embedding_api_pulse.html) through connected apps.


The tradeoff is the setup. Pulse only reports on metrics someone has defined, so it finds changes inside your KPIs, not new questions. Tableau Next’s proactive agent is listed as[“coming soon”](https://www.tableau.com/2026-3-features) , not generally available.


## ThoughtSpot: best for KPI alerts with driver analysis on live warehouse data


**Best for:** teams that want anomaly alerts on live Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery data with change analysis. **Not ideal for:** buyers who want an AI digest without defining KPIs.


ThoughtSpot’s pushed features are[KPI Monitor](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/monitor) alerts and, since release 26.11,[Spotter scheduled updates](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/notes) : a user types “Send me updates on this answer every Monday” and Spotter emails or posts to Slack on that schedule. Anomaly alerts compare values against[ML models trained on the data](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/monitor-alert-anomaly) .[AI Highlights](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/liveboard-ai-highlights) summarizes KPI changes on a Liveboard, but only when a user clicks the button.[SpotIQ change analysis](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/spotiq-change) identifies the attributes that drove a change and writes LLM narratives.


- **Pricing:** Essentials $25/user/month (5 to 50 users) includes automated KPI monitoring and alerts; Pro $50/user/month adds AI highlights, automated change analysis, SAML, and 25 Spotter queries per user per month; both billed annually ([pricing](https://www.thoughtspot.com/pricing) , verified November 14, 2026). A[14-day trial](https://www.thoughtspot.com/trial) needs no card.
- **Cadence and channels:** anomaly checks from every few minutes to monthly, with admins able to cap the fastest frequency (hourly by default). Email, Slack (early access),[webhooks](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/monitor-webhooks) , mobile push, and Teams through the[communication service](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.10.0.cl/communication-service) , which is cloud only.
- **Deployment and data:** ThoughtSpot Cloud or self-managed ThoughtSpot Software;[live queries](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/connections) to Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, PostgreSQL, and others.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/security-rls) applies to KPI alert subscriptions;[SCIM](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/group-user-management-scim) supported.
- **Embedding:** Visual Embed SDK, with an[AI Highlights action](https://developers.thoughtspot.com/docs/actions) for embedded Liveboards.


The AI-written narratives mostly live inside the product. What reaches your inbox by default is an alert, not a written briefing.


## AWS Quick Sight: best for anomaly emails on AWS data with metered pricing


**Best for:** AWS-centric teams that want ML anomaly alerts billed by usage. **Not ideal for:** multi-tenant or departmental data protected by row-level security.


[AWS Quick Sight](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/what-is.html) , formerly Amazon QuickSight and now a feature within AWS Quick, uses the Random Cut Forest algorithm for anomaly detection. An author adds an[anomaly insight](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/anomaly-detection-adding-anomaly-insights.html) with at least one date, measure, and dimension to a published dashboard, and it recalculates hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.[Alert emails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/subscriber-alerts.html) show the total anomaly count and detail the top five, with top contributors. LLM-written[executive summaries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/use-executive-summaries.html) exist but are generated when a user clicks Summarize, not pushed.


- **Pricing:** Reader $3, Reader Pro $20, Author $24, and Author Pro $40 per user/month, with a $250/month infrastructure fee once any Pro user exists. Alerts and anomaly detection cost $0.50 per 1,000 metrics evaluated for the first million ([pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/quick/quicksight/pricing/) , verified November 14, 2026). Executive summaries need Pro roles.
- **Channels:** email. Native Slack or Teams delivery for alerts is not documented.
- **Deployment and data:** AWS cloud only; SPICE or direct query against Redshift, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, and PostgreSQL.
- **Security:**[anomaly detection is not supported](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/restrict-access-to-a-data-set-using-row-level-security.html) for datasets that use row-level security. SAML and SCIM come through IAM Identity Center.
- **Embedding:** dashboards and executive summaries can be embedded through the API.


## Power BI: best for Microsoft shops that already email reports


**Best for:** organizations on Fabric or Premium capacity that already send report subscriptions. **Not ideal for:** teams on Pro licenses only, or anyone who needs per-recipient data in the summary.


Power BI’s pushed AI text is[Summary by Copilot (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-summaries-in-subscriptions) in standard email subscriptions, sent daily, weekly, or monthly. It summarizes what is on the report canvas, does not accept custom prompts, and runs on behalf of the subscription owner, so every recipient sees the owner’s view. It isn’t available for dynamic per-recipient subscriptions, paginated reports, or dashboards.[Anomaly detection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-visualization-anomaly-detection) in line charts includes explanations but stays inside the report.[Data alerts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-set-data-alerts) work only on gauges, KPIs, and cards.


- **Pricing:** Pro $14 and Premium Per User $24 per user/month, paid yearly ([pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) , verified November 14, 2026). Copilot requires[F2+ Fabric or P1+ capacity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-introduction) ; Pro or PPU alone is not enough, and Copilot requests consume capacity units. The 60-day Fabric trial excludes Copilot.
- **Channels:** the Copilot summary is email only. Fabric Activator alerts can go to email or Teams.
- **Deployment and data:** Power BI service only (Report Server is not supported for these AI features); import, DirectQuery, or live connection to Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and PostgreSQL.
- **Security:** sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID; row-level security applies to the subscription owner, not each recipient.
- **Embedding:** the Copilot narrative visual can be embedded (app-owns-data embedding is in preview).


## Zoho Analytics: best for automatic key driver analysis on a small budget


**Best for:** small and midsize teams that want narrative insights and multi-channel alerts at a low published price. **Not ideal for:** buyers who need the AI narrative itself pushed on a schedule.


[Zia Insights](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/zia/insights.html) combines ML analysis with a language model that writes a plain-language summary, and runs key driver analysis automatically for time-series insights. It opens when a user clicks the Zia Insights button. What gets pushed is a[data alert](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/data-alert.html) : a condition or detected anomaly checked every 1 to 12 hours, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.


- **Pricing:** Basic $24/month (2 users), Standard $48 (5 users), Premium $115 (15 users), Enterprise $455 (50 users), billed annually ([pricing](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/pricing.html) , verified November 14, 2026). Data alerts start on Standard (10 alerts); Zia Insights needs Premium. Free plan for 2 users; 15-day trial.
- **Channels:** email, in-app, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and webhooks on a single alert.
- **Deployment and data:** cloud or on-premise; imported data by default, with Live Connect for Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL on higher plans.
- **Security:** row-level security through filter variables; SAML through Zoho Directory. SCIM for Zoho Analytics specifically is not documented.
- **Embedding:** embed snippets, API, and JavaScript SDK, with a flag to expose Zia Insights in embeds.


## Omni: best for scheduled AI answers grounded in a semantic model


**Best for:** data teams with an Omni semantic model who want plain-language reports on a schedule or condition. **Not ideal for:** buyers who need public pricing or Teams delivery.


[AI Routines](https://docs.omni.co/ai/routines) , launched in July 2026, run a prompt through the Omni Agent and deliver “a written, plain-language response” instead of a refreshed dashboard. Schedule mode runs on a cron schedule; condition mode checks a plain-language condition (a threshold, missing data, or a change since the last check) and runs only when it’s met. Each run compiles through Omni’s semantic layer, so metric definitions stay consistent.


- **Pricing:** no public price list. AI usage rolls up into credits, with overage at[$1.00 per credit](https://docs.omni.co/ai/settings/usage) (verified November 14, 2026). Trials are by request.
- **Channels:** email, Slack, or a webhook, one destination per routine.
- **Deployment and data:** Omni-hosted on AWS or Azure; live queries to Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and PostgreSQL.
- **Security:** access filters for row-level security; SAML and SCIM.
- **Embedding:** iframe embedding with an embeddable Omni Agent, but external embed users can’t create routines.


Routines report what you ask about. They don’t look for problems on their own unless the prompt tells them to.


## Databricks Genie: best value if your data already lives in Unity Catalog


**Best for:** Databricks customers who want scheduled AI briefings at no license cost. **Not ideal for:** teams whose data is mostly outside Databricks.


[Genie One scheduled tasks](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie-one/chat) take a natural-language request, such as a daily briefing on new customer reviews, run it at a set time, and email the results with charts and a PDF.[Dashboard Insights](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dashboards/genie-spaces) (beta) surfaces trends, outliers, and top drivers on a published dashboard, but only when a viewer asks. Rule-based[SQL alerts](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/user/alerts/) cover thresholds.


- **Pricing:** Genie One and Genie Agents usage by users is[free through January 31, 2027](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie/) ; service principals are billed and SQL warehouse compute still applies. A trial includes up to[$400 in usage](https://www.databricks.com/try-databricks) (verified November 14, 2026).
- **Channels:** scheduled tasks deliver by email and to a chat thread. Alerts and dashboard subscriptions can go to Slack, Teams, webhooks, and PagerDuty.
- **Deployment and data:** managed on AWS, Azure, and GCP; Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and PostgreSQL reachable through Lakehouse Federation.
- **Security:** Genie evaluates access as the user’s own identity in Unity Catalog, with row filters and column masks; SAML or OIDC and SCIM.
- **Embedding:** Genie Agents embed by iframe for signed-in users only.


## Basedash: best for insights nobody thought to ask for


**Best for:** teams without a dedicated analyst who want an AI to look across their data and report what changed. **Not ideal for:** organizations that need Teams delivery, per-recipient row-level security on every insight, or a free tier.


[Basedash Insights](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/insights) is a feed of AI-written posts about what changed in your data and why it matters, each with a chart. Nobody writes prompts or picks metrics: the AI searches across every connected source it can query, reads your organization’s AI context and recent posts so it doesn’t repeat itself, and decides what is worth a post. Admins can steer it with focus areas. For questions you do know,[automations](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/automations) run your instructions on a schedule or when a SQL query returns new rows, checked every 15 minutes, and can be told to send only when a condition is met.


- **Pricing:** Startup is $1,000/month plus AI usage, with up to 25 users and $1,000/month in AI credits; Enterprise is custom ([pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) , verified November 14, 2026). Insights and automations are on both plans and count toward AI usage. 14-day trial with no credit card; no free plan.
- **Cadence and channels:** Insights generate every day, every weekday, weekly, or monthly, at most one scheduled post per day, to email recipients in your organization and a Slack channel. Automations deliver to email or Slack. Microsoft Teams is not supported.
- **Deployment and data:** cloud, or[self-hosted](https://www.basedash.com/docs/self-hosting/overview) on Enterprise. Live queries against[Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server](https://www.basedash.com/docs/data-sources/introduction) , and more, plus 750+ SaaS sources through Basedash Warehouse.
- **Security:** Insights run with the access of the organization’s earliest active admin, and every member can read every insight, so sensitive topics belong in an automation shared with specific people. Automations run as their creator, including[row-level security](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/row-level-security) , which Basedash supports on Postgres and Supabase only.[SSO](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/sso) and SCIM are Enterprise features.
- **Embedding:** Enterprise[full app embedding](https://www.basedash.com/docs/developers/embedding) can show or hide Insights or open a specific post.


Examples are on the[Insights feature page](https://www.basedash.com/features/insights) and[automations feature page](https://www.basedash.com/features/automations) . For statistical anomaly detection with per-user governance, ThoughtSpot or Tableau Pulse fits better.


## Which augmented analytics tool should you choose?


**If your KPIs are already defined and governed:** Tableau Pulse sends the cleanest metric digests, with statistics a person can audit and the AI limited to wording. ThoughtSpot is the alternative on live warehouse data, with more alert types and driver analysis.


**If you want daily insights in Slack instead of manual SQL dashboards:** Basedash Insights, Omni Routines, and ThoughtSpot Spotter updates all post to Slack. Basedash needs no prompt; Omni and ThoughtSpot report on the question you set.


**If you need AI-written summaries, not just alerts:** Basedash, Omni, Databricks Genie, and Power BI push language-model text. Tableau Pulse adds an AI summary to a statistical digest. ThoughtSpot, Zoho, and Quick Sight keep their narratives mostly in-app.


**If row-level security must apply per recipient:** Tableau Pulse and ThoughtSpot evaluate each user’s security context. Power BI summaries and Basedash automations run as one account, and Quick Sight anomaly detection doesn’t work on RLS datasets.


**If price is the deciding factor:** Databricks Genie has no user fee through January 2027 if your data is already there. Zoho Analytics publishes the lowest paid plans. Quick Sight meters alerts by metric evaluated.


**If you use Microsoft Teams:** Tableau Pulse, ThoughtSpot, Zoho, and Databricks alerts deliver there; Basedash and Omni routines do not.


For alerting on specific metric thresholds, see our comparison of[BI tools for AI anomaly detection and smart alerting](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-for-ai-anomaly-detection-and-smart-alerting-2026) . For agents that also take actions, see[AI agents for data analysis compared](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-ai-agents-for-data-analysis-agentic-analytics-tools-2026) , and for a head-to-head on one of these tools,[Basedash vs ThoughtSpot](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-thoughtspot) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What are augmented analytics tools?


Augmented analytics tools use machine learning or language models to do parts of an analyst’s work: finding anomalies, explaining which factors drove a change, writing summaries, or answering plain-language questions. The term covers on-demand features like chat and proactive ones that push findings to email, Slack, or Teams. Tableau Pulse, ThoughtSpot, Zoho Analytics, AWS Quick Sight, and Power BI Copilot are common examples. They differ on whether you must define metrics first, whether a language model or a statistical model finds the insight, and who receives it.


### Which AI data analyst can Slack me daily insights instead of manual SQL dashboards?


Basedash Insights can post to a Slack channel every day or every weekday without anyone writing a prompt or choosing metrics; the AI decides what changed and writes it up with a chart. Omni AI Routines post a written answer to a prompt you define, on a schedule or when a condition is met. ThoughtSpot Spotter can send scheduled updates on a saved answer to Slack. Tableau Pulse digests also reach Slack, but only for metrics someone has defined. Databricks Genie scheduled tasks deliver by email rather than Slack.


### What are the pros and cons of LLM-powered insights versus traditional BI for support teams?


LLM-powered insights explain changes in plain language, such as a spike in tickets tied to one product area, and can cover questions nobody built a dashboard for. They save support leads from checking dashboards daily. The downsides are less predictability, since wording and focus vary between runs, and permission scope, since many scheduled AI runs use one account’s data access. Traditional BI dashboards and threshold alerts are deterministic and easier to audit. Many teams pair the two: rule-based alerts for SLA breaches, and an AI digest for trends in ticket volume, tags, and satisfaction.


### How do generative AI assistants in BI software surface market trends faster than traditional workflows?


In a traditional workflow, an analyst notices a change, writes queries, builds a chart, and shares it, which can take days. Generative AI assistants shorten that by running the analysis on a schedule and delivering the result. Tableau Pulse detects trend changes statistically and has AI summarize them in a digest. ThoughtSpot SpotIQ identifies the attributes that drove a change. Basedash Insights searches connected data for new patterns and posts them with a chart. Speed still depends on data freshness: an AI digest is only as current as the last warehouse load.


### Which reporting tools generate natural language summaries automatically?


Power BI adds a Copilot-written summary to scheduled email subscriptions (in preview, on F2 or P1 capacity and above). Tableau Pulse puts an AI-written insight summary at the top of each metric digest. Omni Routines, Databricks Genie scheduled tasks, and Basedash automations return a written analysis of a prompt on each run, and Basedash Insights writes posts without a prompt. Zoho Analytics Zia Insights and AWS Quick Sight executive summaries write narratives too, but a user has to open them in the product.


### Can AI tools surface insights without manual dashboard setup?


Most cannot. Tableau Pulse needs metric definitions, ThoughtSpot needs KPI charts, AWS Quick Sight needs an anomaly widget on a published dashboard, and Power BI summarizes an existing report. Omni Routines and Databricks Genie scheduled tasks skip dashboards but need a written prompt. Basedash Insights is the exception in this comparison: after an admin turns it on and chooses a cadence, the AI queries the connected data sources and decides what to report, with an optional focus-area field to steer it.


### What should I monitor in an AI-driven BI tool to spot shifts in operational health in real time?


Start with a short list of leading indicators that move before revenue does, such as order volume, fulfillment time, error rates, support ticket volume, and active users, and set thresholds on the ones with known limits. Check frequency matters more than the AI layer: ThoughtSpot anomaly checks can run every few minutes if an admin lowers the hourly default cap, Basedash data-change automations check every 15 minutes, Zoho alerts run as often as hourly, and Tableau Pulse alerts are checked once a day. Use anomaly detection for metrics with seasonality, and an unprompted AI digest to catch shifts outside your list.


### Do automated AI insights respect row-level security?


It depends on the tool. Tableau Pulse generates insights in each user’s data security context, and ThoughtSpot applies row-level security to KPI alert subscriptions. Power BI Copilot summaries run on behalf of the subscription owner, so all recipients see the owner’s data. Basedash automations run with their creator’s access, including row-level security, while Basedash Insights run as the earliest active admin and are visible to every member. AWS Quick Sight anomaly detection is not supported on datasets that use row-level security.
